detail.longDescription: Every time I run jekyll build for some reason the CSS is always cached. If I run jekyll serve --livereload the site builds with cached CSS then if I change a file, the live reload updates all of the CSS. Currently the only way to push updated code to my Netlify instance is to run jekyll serve --livereload , update a file and copy everything from the _site folder, which seems silly and counterintuitive. Plus my client would like to run jekyll build as they normally would. I have tried adding this: {% assign cacheVersion = site.time | date:'?v=%s' %} <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ "/assets/css/style.css" | prepend: site.baseurl | append: cacheVersion }}"> This seems to truncate the current time integer by a few digits For example '1794661783' which translates to 'Wed Jan 21 1970 19:31:01 GMT+0100 (Greenwich Mean Time)' I am seeing variations of this but it's always 1970. So I tried a pure JS solution like so: // append css with todays date as integer and version const now = new Date().getTime(); const head = document.querySelector('head'); const template = <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/style.css?v=${now}">; head.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', template); Same net result the URL looks like it is updated: <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/style.css?v=1794661953231"> but the CSS is still cached. I've tried updating html markup in include layouts (header.html, footer.html), as well as adding a javascript logger. Both the updated markup and the logger work and are showing as updated. So it only seems to be CSS caching for some reason. Then I wondered about trying to disable sass-cache. In the config.yml I have tried sass: cache: false As per https://github.com/jekyll/jekyll-sass-converter/issues/36 sass: cache: --no-cache As per Cannot disable SASS cache Neither seems to have worked. Although I can't find anything about disabling sass-cache for Jekyll specifically, even so I don't think this would resolve the issue. Any pointers?
